subject: physics
question_text: Write the physical quantities that have J m⁻¹ and J m⁻² as their units.

recall_prompt: Say the steps you would write for this answer, in order. You can speak in English, in Telugu, or in both.

page_header: Section A — Very Short Answer Question

steps.label: J m⁻¹
lines: J m⁻¹ is energy divided by length.

lines.text: J m⁻¹ = N  ⇒ the quantity is FORCE

steps.why: Rearranging W = F s gives F = W/s, so joule per metre is only another way of writing the newton.
common_mistakes: Answering "energy" or "work". Those have the unit J, not J m⁻¹.

recall.must_convey: That joule per metre is the newton, so the quantity is force.

steps.memory_tip: Work = force × distance, so energy ÷ length is force.
steps.margin_note: Show W = F s. The rearrangement is the reason.

steps.label: J m⁻²
lines: J m⁻² is energy divided by area.
Its value equals the surface tension of the
liquid, whose unit N m⁻¹ is the same thing.
steps.why: J m⁻² and N m⁻¹ are the same combination written two ways, which is exactly why surface energy and surface tension have equal numerical values.
common_mistakes: Answering "pressure". Pressure is N m⁻², not J m⁻².

recall.must_convey: That joule per square metre is surface energy, equal in value to surface tension.

steps.memory_tip: J m⁻² = N m⁻¹, which is why surface energy and surface tension share a number.
steps.margin_note: Naming both surface energy and surface tension is safest.

insider_note: Asked in AP March 2026. Energy per length is force; energy per area is surface tension’s partner, surface energy.
